thread.title: Apple Warns: Key Takeaways - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Apple Warns: Key Takeaways - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
After the bell on Wednesday, technology giant Apple ( AAPL ) reported preliminary fiscal first quarter results that badly missed estimates, sending the tech sector and US market futures quite lower in the after-hours. The company cited iPhone weakness as the main culprit, primarily due to a major sales shortfall in China. With the stock getting pummeled as seen below, I'm here today to provide my key takeaways from this unfortunate news.
( Source: cnbc.com)
The major news was that management now sees the December quarter's revenue at about $84 billion, well below the previous guidance it issued, which was a range of $89 billion to $93 billion. Gross margins and operating expenses are expected to be at the lower end of their ranges, while other income items will be about $250 million better than previously forecast. Obviously this is a big miss, with the street average being about $91.5 billion going into this news, having declined a bit in recent weeks as seen below.
The first key takeaway is that China is a major problem. Not only is the economy there slowing, but trade tensions and threats of further tariffs have not helped the overall situation. Management stated that traffic to Apple retail stores in China has been soft, and the contraction in the smartphone market has been rather steep. Falling stock markets also has reduced consumer sentiment, further weighing on overall sales.
The second key thing I'd like to highlight basically echoes some of the key themes I've discussed with Apple in my coverage of the name over the last few quarters. Take a look at some of the key phrases detailed in the warning:
In some developed markets, iPhone upgrades also were not as strong as we thought they would be. Some customers taking advantage of significantly reduced pricing for iPhone battery replacements. I've been talking for some time now about how consumers might not be too happy with Apple's rising price structure , and it looks like that is coming true. Also, I've brought up the iPhone battery replacement program several times over the last year, because why get a new $749 or more expensive phone if you can just replace your battery for $29? Making phones too costly and too large is a main reason why I said in my most recent article that Apple needs to revisit its iPhone strategy in 2019. While I didn't think a new version of the iPhone SE was coming, arguing Apple could take a middle ground approach, today's warning makes me wonder if Apple will again try a smaller, lower cost phone at some point this year.
Another key item to look at is that outside of the iPhone, the business is still quite strong. Non-iPhone revenues were up about 19% in the period, with the services segment generating over $10.8 billion in total sales. Records were set in services, wearables (up more than 50%) and Mac. Also, despite the significant sales shortfall, gross margins still were forecast to be around the low end of the previous range, meaning Apple wasn't forced to lower prices and it didn't see a major shift in sales mix to lower margin products. I would have been really worried if gross margin guidance had been cut say 100 or 150 basis points with revenues coming in this low.
The company also expects to set a new quarterly EPS record, thanks to the buyback, increased income items, and of course a much lower tax rate than the year ago period thanks to US tax cuts. Apple expects to have a net cash position of $130 billion at the end of the period, up about $7 billion sequentially. It will be interesting to see how much was spent on share repurchases as a result, but the December quarter generally is the biggest cash generation period of the year for Apple. Unfortunately, the buyback is significantly underwater in recent quarters thanks to the sharp decline in shares. In the coming days, Apple will likely be back to Spring/Summer 2017 levels as seen below.
( Source: Yahoo! Finance)
The question now turns to the near future. How low will guidance be for the fiscal second quarter which ends in March?
Management is guiding for a roughly 4.85% revenue decline in fiscal Q1, and the street was expecting accelerating growth in Q2 of 5.1%. It's likely that economic weakness will pick up a bit unless the US/China trade war ends soon, along with the US government shutdown not helping. Plus, the reversal of iPhone launches from lower to higher prices last year with the iPhone X being later set a higher bar for the current period, where this year's XS/XS Max went on sale a lot earlier. It would thus not surprise me to see guidance somewhere in a range of a 6% to 10% decline, meaning perhaps $58 billion or so at the low end.
With Apple down about 7.5% in the after-hours session, the stock is basically at a 2.00% annual dividend yield point. The fall in shares is spreading to most of the tech sector, and the market overall looks to be down about 2% on Thursday. However, given that we are well off of the December lows, a retest of those levels likely would push Apple down towards $140 or perhaps even lower. The only good news is at those prices you are getting a higher dividend yield and the buyback will be a lot more powerful.
While I have been a little nervous regarding Apple in the last couple of months, the magnitude of Wednesday's warning did surprise me a bit. China is obviously the main culprit, and unless the trade war rhetoric is calmed down soon this problem will probably linger for a few more quarters. Also, it does seem like higher iPhone pricing and the battery replacement program did impact phone sales a bit more than management was expecting. Perhaps that will provide a lesson moving forward, allowing for a better smartphone lineup this year or next. Should US markets retest last month lows, we could see Apple shares down almost $100 from their highs. Once the dust settles and we see where expectations level out, we can then discuss whether it is time to start buying again.
